words: إن ربك هو يفصل بينهم يوم القيامة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about some people among them going astray leads into reassurance for believers and a threat to unbelievers, as a renewed warning to deniers of resurrection.
rows.anchor: أنه كان منهم من يضل عن أمر الله ويصد عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God the Prophet’s Lord recalls His beneficence in sending him and signals the honor he will receive at Judgment, including the Praised Station.
rows.anchor: المحسن إليك بإرسالك ليعظم ثوابك ويعلي ما بك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone will judge truthfully among the guided, those who mislead, and the astray, raising the wronged and ruining the oppressor’s plot.
rows.anchor: فيعلى أمر المظلوم ويردي كيد الظالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their disputes are innate and continually renewed; nothing in them is hidden from God.
rows.anchor: يجددون الاختلاف فيه على سبيل الاستمرار حسب ما طبعوا عيله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God judges disputed matters between the parties; other matters are judged for or against them, while disagreement that was not deliberate falls under pardon.
rows.anchor: ما اختلفوا فيه لا على وجه القصد فيقع في محل العفو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra has two denials, of the Qur’an and resurrection; God answers them with paired rejecting questions and distinct endings, making four interrogative forms.
rows.anchor: أتبعه استفهامين إنكاريين منشورين على القولين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains يهْدِ as making clear or showing the way; Biqāʿī attributes this gloss to a report in al-Bukhārī.
rows.anchor: كما رواه البخاري عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

words: كم أهلكنا من قبلهم من القرون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Past peoples were destroyed for opposing messengers, while those who believed in the signs were saved.
rows.anchor: الماضين من المعرضين عن الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nearby ruins make the warning vivid: proximity in place can recall the past as strongly as proximity in time through repeated encounters with traces.
rows.anchor: لكثرة التذكير بالآثار , والتردد خلال الديار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their intense attachment to sensory things means they reflect only while walking through the dwellings of ʿĀd, Thamūd, Lot’s people, and similar nations.
rows.anchor: لشدة ارتباطهم مع المحسوسات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ruins and other traces are visible signs, while reports of the destroyed peoples are audible signs.
rows.anchor: مرئيات في الديار وغيرها من الآثار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearing is the chief means by which news of the destroyed peoples reached the audience; the warning itself should suffice to turn them from error.
rows.anchor: وكان إهلاك القرون إنما وصل إليهم بالسماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If those who hear the account still do not turn back, they are effectively without hearing.
rows.anchor: في الرجوع عن الغي إلى غير سماعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question rebukes those who deny resurrection by pointing to God’s sending water to revive barren land.
rows.anchor: أيقولون في إنكار البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sends the water from either the sky or the earth.
rows.anchor: من السماء أو الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-jarz is land whose growth has been cut away by drying and crushing, leaving a smooth surface without vegetation.
rows.anchor: أي التي جزر نباتها أي قطع باليبس والتهشم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says al-jarz is land where rain falls but is too scant to benefit it; Biqāʿī cites al-Bukhārī for the report.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : إنها التي لا تمطر إلا مطرا لا يغني عنها شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Water draws plants from the earth’s depths by mixing with the soil; their emergence is real, not an illusion like a magician’s trick.
rows.anchor: أي نبتا لا ساق له باختلاط الماء بالتراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What livestock eat includes the crop’s grain, leaves, straw, and grasses; livestock come first because they sustain people’s livelihoods and bodies, and the passage concerns vegetation generally.
rows.anchor: أي من حبه وورقه وتبنه وحشيشه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike ʿAbasa, this passage names livestock first because it treats vegetation generally; ʿAbasa follows food through to the human meal and lists foods unsuitable for livestock.
rows.anchor: فإن السياق لطعام الإنسان الذي هو نهاية الزرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People eat the crop’s grain and its root when it is still green fodder.
rows.anchor: من حبه , وأصله إذا كان بقلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The visible revival of barren land plainly proves resurrection; one who sees its evidence and persists in denial lacks sight and insight.
rows.anchor: على ما فيها من الدلالة وأصر على الإنكار لا بصر له ولا بصيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording clarifies that the favor comes from God alone, not through an intermediary as its source; the indefinite form magnifies the favor.
rows.anchor: بين أن الأمر ليس إلا منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The favor also shows that no created thing can be brought into being independently of God’s will.
rows.anchor: وأنه لا يتوقف تكوين شيء على غير إرادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addressing mountains as rational beings who promptly obey dramatizes God’s complete power and control of all things.
rows.anchor: الجبال منزلة العقلاء الذين يبادرون إلى امتثال أوامره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains echo David’s glorification, recitation of the Psalms, and other remembrance whenever he glorifies God.
rows.anchor: رجعي التسبيح وقراءة الزبور وغيرهما من ذكر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains, the earth’s hardest substance, respond to a command as rational servants; this is an earthly sign of God’s power.
rows.anchor: مما هو أشد الأرض بما هو وظيفة العقلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Birds, the lightest animals and vulnerable to falling if they die in flight, provide a heavenly sign of God’s power over the sky.
rows.anchor: عطف على ذلك أخف الحيوان وألطفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The birds truly echoed David’s remembrance, like the birds’ own speech; their mention rules out the idea that the sound was merely an echo.
rows.anchor: فكانت ترجع معه الذكر فدل قرانها بالطير على ذكرها حقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb reads al-ṭayr in the nominative, coordinating with the form of جبال; other readers coordinate with its syntactic position, while the conjunction may also mean with or imply an elided verb.
rows.anchor: أو تكون الواو بمعنى مع أو بتقدير فعل من معنى ما مضى كسخرنا

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه
rows.claim: Wahb b. Munabbih reports that David told the mountains to glorify and the birds to answer, then sang beautifully while reciting the Psalms.
rows.anchor: قال وهب بن منبه : كان يقول للجبال : سبحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī adduces reports that pebbles glorified in the hands of the Prophet, Abū Bakr, and ʿUmar, and that food glorified while being eaten in the Prophet’s presence.
rows.anchor: وكما كان الطعام يسبح في حضرته الشريفة وهو يؤكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī also recalls reports that a stone greeted the Prophet, the house threshold and walls said amen to his prayer, and the trunk moaned.
rows.anchor: وأسكفة الباب وحوائط البيت تؤمن على دعائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī adds reports that a lizard testified for the Prophet and that a camel complained when its eggs were taken, so the Prophet ordered them returned out of mercy.
rows.anchor: وكما كان الضب يشهد له والجمل يشكو أخذ بيضها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made iron, which originated in the mountains, as pliable in David’s hand as wax, so he could shape it without fire or hammer.
rows.anchor: الذي ولدناه من الجبال جعلناه في يده كالشمع يعمل منه ما يريد بلا نار ولا مطرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to make armor explains the purpose of softening iron and indicates that David’s craft was devoted to God.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكر علة الإلانة بصيغة الأمر إشارة إلى أن عمله كان لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sābighāt are long, ample coats of armor.
rows.anchor: أي دروعا طوالا واسعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sard is the piercing and threading of leather; linking each armor ring to the next resembles stitching through holes with a continuous thread.
rows.anchor: السرد الخزر في الأديم وإدخال الخيط في موضع الخرز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David should make every ring equal and tight enough to stop arrows, secure against swords, and light enough for quick movement and fighting in hot or cold weather.
rows.anchor: أي النسج بأن يكون كل حلقة مساوية لأختها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī thinks the armor rings probably had no rivets: pliable iron made them unnecessary, and rivets would remove the benefit of softening; someone who saw the armor reportedly confirmed this.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه لم يكن في حلقها مسامير لعدم الحاجة بإلانة الحديد إليها

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj defines sard as measuring one thing to fit the next so that the parts follow in orderly succession, as in telling a story.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : السرد في اللغة : تقدير الشيء إلى الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī compares David’s softened iron with the Prophet’s miraculous softening of the trench obstruction: one account says a single blow broke it, another says water made it loose sand.
rows.anchor: وهذا كما ألان الله تعالى للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في الخندق تلك الكدية وفي رواية

rows.speaker: سلمان
rows.claim: Salman reported that picks and axes failed against a rock at the trench; the Prophet broke it with three blows, each illuminating Medina, and announced the future conquests of Ṣanʿāʾ, al-Ḥīra, and Syria.
rows.anchor: تلك الصخرة التي أخبره سلمان رضي الله عنها أنها كسرت فؤوسهم ومعاولهم وعجزوا عنها فضربها النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ثلاث ضربات

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن جحش
rows.claim: Biqāʿī cites a report, noted by al-Kilāʿī from al-Zubayr b. Abī Bakr and al-Bayhaqī, that the Prophet turned ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaḥsh’s broken Uhud sword into a palm rib sword called al-ʿAwn, later sold for 200 dinars.
rows.anchor: سيف عبد الله بن جحش رضي الله عنه انقطع يوم أحد , فأعطاه رسول الله

rows.speaker: عكاشة بن محصن
rows.claim: At Badr, the Prophet gave ʿUkāsha b. Miḥṣan a piece of wood when his sword broke; it became a long, strong, bright sword, which he carried in later campaigns until his death in the Ridda.
rows.anchor: وقاتل عكاشة بن محصن يوم بدر فانقطع سيفه

rows.speaker: الواقدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāqidī reports that when Salama b. Aslam b. al-Ḥuraysh’s sword broke at Badr, the Prophet gave him a date-palm twig that became a fine sword, kept until Salama died at the Battle of the Bridge.
rows.anchor: وعن الواقدي أنه انكسر سيف سلمة بن أسلم بن الحريش يوم بدر فأعطاه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: معوذ بن عفراء
rows.claim: Biqāʿī cites al-Bayhaqī and others on the Prophet restoring Muʿawwidh b. ʿAfrāʾ’s severed hand after Abū Jahl cut it at Badr; it healed as before.
rows.anchor: وإلحامه للحديد ليس بأعجب من إلحام النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ليد معوذ بن عفراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural command turns from favors particular to David to a command that includes him and everyone who obeys him.
rows.anchor: عطف عليها ما جمع فيه الضمير لأنه يعم غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: David and his followers should do right by means of the knowledge and divinely granted success to obey that God has given them.
rows.anchor: أي بما تفضلنا به عليكم من العلم والتوفيق للطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sees and knows every deed, inward and outward; this assurance encourages obedience and warns against neglect.
rows.anchor: أي مبصر وعالم بكل ظاهر له وباطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic warning answers denials of resurrection, which imply denial of other divine attributes; the negligent act as though they deny that God observes them.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أن إنكارهم للقدرة على البعث إنكار لغيرها من الصفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After establishing truth with decisive proofs and threatening seizure, Biqāʿī argues that punishment presupposes sin; everyone has some burden that warrants it.
rows.anchor: وكان العقاب لا يكون حكمه إلا عند الذنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one is punished at resurrection or during seizure by carrying another’s sin; each is liable only for what that person committed.
rows.anchor: لا تحمل حاملة من جهة الإثم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse says a sin-bearing soul, rather than simply a soul, because no soul fit to bear a burden is free of a burden of its own; only God protects from sin.
rows.anchor: ولما لم تكن نفس متأهلة للحمل تخلو من وزر تحمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each person has deeds, directly or causally, that establish the case against that person; no one is seized for another’s personal sin, unlike worldly tyrants.
rows.anchor: لا تؤخذ نفس بذنب أخرى الذي يخصها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even a soul weighed down by disbelief or other sins cannot get another person to carry any part of its uniquely personal burden to lessen its punishment.
rows.anchor: أي بالذنوب سواء كانت كفرا أو غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one carries any portion of the burden, willingly or by compulsion.
rows.anchor: أي لا طواعية ولا كرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kinship gives no exemption, whether the relative is the one calling for help or the one asked to carry the burden.
rows.anchor: ذلك الداعي أو المدعو للحمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first statement says no one is destroyed for another’s sin; the second says no one’s own sin is removed for another to save them.
rows.anchor: أنه لا يهلك أحد بذنب غيره بل بذنب نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the rule is clear, it is heart-rending; one wonders at anyone who hears it without fear. Only those who benefit from turning back are effectively its audience.
rows.anchor: أي إنذارا يفيد الرجوع عن الغي , فلاختصاصهم بالنفع كانوا كأنهم مختصون بالإنذار

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayrī defines warning as informing someone of the place of danger.
rows.anchor: القشيري : الإعلام بموضع المخافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect form depicts fear practiced now and maintained into the future.
rows.anchor: أي يوقعون هذا الفعل في الحال يواظبون عليه في الاستقبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wisest fear their benefactor, since even a small punishment could end His beneficence.
rows.anchor: أعقل الناس من خاف المحسن لأن أقل عقابه قطع إحسانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may mean that they fear what remains unseen, or that they fear God while unseen by anyone who might otherwise witness their devotion.
rows.anchor: حال كونه غائبا عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The highest believers remain sincere in private and public, trusting the messenger’s report of unseen matters without needing a miracle or unveiling.
rows.anchor: من كانت غيبته مثل حضوره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī says he knows no one who matched Khadīja and al-Ṣiddīq in this sincere faith in the unseen.
rows.anchor: ولا نعلم أحدا وازى خديجة والصديق رضي الله عنهما في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer gathers inward and outward submission and is the noblest worship.
rows.anchor: الصلاة جامعة لخضوع الظاهر والباطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Establishing prayer means guarding all its limits at all times, a strong sign of sincerity; its past tense suits the fixed prayer times, five prayers and their associated sunnas.
rows.anchor: وكانت إقامتها بمعنى حفظ جميع حدودها في كل حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazakkā means to purify oneself and increase in these virtues; its form suggests the great effort needed to overcome the soul’s pull toward defilement.
rows.anchor: أي تطهر وتكثر بهذه المحاسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī supplies an implied contrast: the corrupt person’s defilement harms only that person, just as the purified person’s growth benefits that person.
rows.anchor: ومن تدسى فإنما يتدسى على نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purification benefits the person who undertakes it; emphasis is needed because people may overlook that the benefit is specifically their own.
rows.anchor: قد يغفل عن أن هذا نفع له وخاص به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All return to God, who fully discloses His attributes in the resurrection and recompenses each person’s deeds, vindicating the Prophet against those who accept or reject his warning.
rows.anchor: الذي يكشف عن جميع صفاته أتم كشف تحتمله العقول يوم البعث لا إلى غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparisons illustrate the unequal states of the morally corrupt and purified, and what produces corruption or purification; they also affirm divine power against explanations based on nature.
rows.anchor: فما يستوي في الطبع والعقل المتدسي الذي هو أعمى بعصيانه في الظلمات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blind and seeing exemplify unbeliever and believer, and ignorant and learned; the blind is named first because ignorance precedes the sending of revelation.
rows.anchor: مثالا للكافر والمؤمن والجاهل والعالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison denies equality in every respect, not shared humanity or every basic feature; people differ even within each class.
rows.anchor: أي في حالة من الأحوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blind people vary greatly: some navigate difficult streets unaided while others cannot cross their homes; some can infer writing or identify counterfeit coins and regional mints by touch.
rows.anchor: فتجد بعض العمى يمشي بلا قائد في الأزقة المشكلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Differences among sighted people are also plain; unequal abilities show that a free agent adds distinctions to creation, rather than nature making every individual alike.
rows.anchor: وأما البصراء فالأمر فيهم واضح في المفاوتة في أبصارهم وبصائرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī says the form iftiʿāl here has the sense of mutuality; it may stress denied equality despite any effort to achieve it, or deny equality in every respect.
rows.anchor: لأن افتعل هنا لمعنى تفاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the negative emphasizes the contrast because differences among kinds of darkness and light are less immediately apparent; sins darken a believer’s heart even when the person sees.
rows.anchor: وأكد بتكرير النافي كالذي قبله لأن المفارقة بين أفراد الظلمة وأفراد النور خفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Darkness represents falsehood and light represents truth; the many routes of error are hard to count, but the path of truth is one, against the heretical claim that paths to God equal the number of creatures’ breaths.
rows.anchor: من الزنادقة : الطرق إلى الله بعدد أنفاس الخلائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone created these opposites and varied each kind: sunlight, moonlight, starlight, and lamplight differ, as do shadows of different density.
rows.anchor: فما أبدعهما على هذا التضاد إلا الله تعالى الفاعل المختار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shade comes first because darkness grows from shadows, which remove light; its ordering also fits the priority of mercy over wrath.
rows.anchor: عن الظلال , وهو نسخ النور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cool shade represents the believer’s refuge in the afterlife, while scorching heat represents the disbeliever’s destination.
rows.anchor: ببرده الذي هو مرجع المؤمن في الآخرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās defines al-ḥarūr as a hot wind at night; Biqāʿī cites al-Baghawī for the report.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : هي الريح الحارة بالليل

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qāmūs adds that al-ḥarūr can also refer to daytime, the heat of the sun, continual heat, or fire.
rows.anchor: في القاموس وزاد : وقد يكون بالنهار وحر الشمس والحر الدائم والنار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Life comes first because it is what manifests the differences under discussion.
rows.anchor: المظهر لذلك كله الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse repeats the verb, going beyond the blind-and-seeing example because blind people still share some perceptions; believers receive two analogies with different rhetorical functions.
rows.anchor: الأعمى يشارك البصير في بعض الإدراكات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Living people differ in speech, intelligence, temperament, and ease of manner; scarcely any two are alike in every trait.
rows.anchor: لأنه منهم الناطق والأعجم , والذكي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dead represent unbelievers and vary in the difficulty of death and decay, as well as in the hidden misery or felicity that unbelievers refuse to acknowledge.
rows.anchor: أي الذين هم مثال للكافرين في صعوبة الموت وسهولته والبلى وغيره مما يخفى ولا يقر به الكفار من الشقاوة والسعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These examples clearly show God’s free agency and the error of associating partners with Him, since nothing resembles Him.
rows.anchor: من وضوح الدلالة على الفعل بالاختيار وعلى ضلال من أشرك به شيئا لأنه لا يشابهه شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives hearing, meaning guidance, to whom He wills and deafens, blinds, overturns, or ruins whom He wills among living hearts and spirits and dead meanings and forms.
rows.anchor: أي فيهديه ولو لم يكن له قابلية في العادة كالجمادات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If response to revelation depended on natural capacity, everyone would accept or reject alike, since the call and displayed miracles reach them on equal terms.
rows.anchor: لأن نسبة الدعوة وإظهار المعجزة إليهم على حد سواء

words: إِنَّمَا تُنذِرُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُم بِٱلْغَيْبِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s selective granting of receptive hearing explains why warning benefits those He wills, confirming the earlier statement that only those who fear God gain from it and consoling the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وإن الإنذار إنما هو لمن قضى بانتفاعه
